newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end little changed, feeders up.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end little changed, feeders up.

text.p: CME live cattle futures lacked direction late and ended lightly mixed awaiting pending indications of cash cattle price direction, traders said.
Feeder cattle futures held their gains, bolstered by lower corn futures, traders said.

October live cattle were pressured by profit taking and bull spread unwinding most of the session on concern packers were holding bids for cash cattle at $71 instead of the $72 to $73 per cwt bids that had been expected. However, feedlots held asking prices firm and early futures sellers covered short positions, traders said.
There was also evening up ahead of the USDA hog report.

Projections that hog numbers will remain under year ago levels into next year can be viewed as supportive for cattle markets, traders said. Cattle numbers are seen rising sometime around the start of next year and which makes beef more competitive with pork until hog numbers start to rise, they said.
Spreading added to early pressure in October before the short covering developed. Rosenthal notably sold October and bought December, they added.
In live cattle options, commission houses bought October 71 puts and there was light spreading of the February 66/68 call spread. Volatility was steady, pit sources said.
Feeder cattle futures remained supported by lower corn futures in thin trade. Prospects of declining feed costs offset recent weakness in cash feeders, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.19 at $63.55 per cwt.
Stone Traders bought October late after early buying by R.J. O'Brien and Refco. Merrill Lynch in locals notably sold, pit sources said.

Live cattle closed 0.075 cent a lb lower to 0.050 higher with October off most at 73.100 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.150 to 0.350 cent higher with October up 0.150 at 63.700 cents. September expired earlier at 63.450 cents, up 0.025 cent for the day.
